summary: Confirmed the dispatch's accumulator diagnosis, and empirically resolved the absorbed-208 pagination discrepancy live against the running Zotero API: annotations are silently dropped from csljson page bodies without shifting pagination windows, so short pages are normal mid-library, not end-of-pagination. Also found two previously-unknown no-op filter bugs: the existing attachment/note CSL-type filter never matches (Zotero emits 'document', not 'attachment'/'note'), and fetch_path3's itemTypeID exclusion list (1,3,28) targets the wrong types entirely (real IDs are 2/26/37) -- so the on-disk 'ground truth' 4042-item export is ~61% non-bibliographic stub entries.

artifacts.summary: Root-cause report covering the accumulator bug, the live-verified pagination-termination bug (resolves absorbed task 208), and two newly-found itemType-filter no-op bugs in fetch_path1 and fetch_path3, with fix recommendations and a flagged user decision on Path 3 scope.

memory_candidates.content: Zotero 7 local API (127.0.0.1:23119): format=csljson pagination windows (start/limit) apply to the RAW item table (including attachment/note/annotation rows), matching Total-Results and the default format=json exactly. But the csljson-CONVERTED page body silently drops annotation-typed rows without adjusting the window or Total-Results, so a mid-library page can legitimately be shorter than `limit`. Any pagination loop must track `start` against Total-Results (or the Link rel=last header), never against the converted array's own length.

Zotero's local-API csljson serializer maps the Zotero itemType 'attachment' to CSL type 'document' (not 'attachment'), and never emits literal 'attachment'/'note' CSL type strings. A filter checking `.type != "attachment" and .type != "note"` against csljson output is a silent no-op. To reliably exclude non-bibliographic items from a csljson export, cross-reference the item's real Zotero itemType via a parallel format=json (raw) fetch, keyed by item key, rather than filtering on the CSL .type field.

To read a Zotero (or any actively-held) sqlite database for inspection while the owning app holds a lock, `sqlite3 -readonly path.sqlite ...` can still fail with 'database is locked'. `sqlite3 "file:path.sqlite?immutable=1" ...` succeeds for one-shot read inspection since it opens assuming no concurrent writer will invalidate the read -- useful for verifying schema/itemType tables without needing to close the app first.

user_decision.note: No blocking decision needed to proceed to planning. One planning-time decision is flagged in the report's Decisions/Recommendations sections (finding 6/7): whether to fix fetch_path3's itemTypeID no-op bug within this task's scope, since it changes the shrink guard's baseline. This is a scoping/judgment call for the planner, not a blocker for research to hand off.
